thought.text: The `.env` is properly configured. Now let me start the Docker Compose infrastructure (background, as `--wait` blocks):

reasoning_content:
`.env` looks correct. The LLM values point to my local stub. The Docling values point to the CPU container I'm about to launch.

Next, I'll start the Docling container (following the guide) and bring up the Docker Compose infrastructure. Since the Docling container requires pulling the image first (large size), I'll start compose in parallel — the infrastructure doesn't depend on Docling.

Procedure:
1. Start `docker compose --env-file .env up --wait` (in the background — it takes time since it's waiting for the health check of all services).
2. Wait for the docling pull to complete, then run the docling container.

Note: `docker compose up --wait` waits for all services to become healthy. Note that the init-type containers (temporal-init, minio-init, keycloak-bootstrap) — keycloak-bootstrap has restart: on-failure, and oauth2-proxy depends on keycloak-bootstrap's `service_completed_successfully`. Let's just run it for now and see what happens.

One concern: the memory limit of 7.6Gi. The Keycloak + Postgres + Temporal stack should fit. I'll monitor it.

Now, I'll start compose up in the background.

action.command:
cd /workspace && nohup bash -c 'docker compose --env-file .env up --wait > /tmp/compose-up.log 2>&1; echo "COMPOSE_EXIT=$?" > /tmp/compose-up.done' &
echo "compose up started, pid $!"
sleep 20
echo "=== compose up log so far ==="; tail -15 /tmp/compose-up.log; echo "=== ps ==="; docker ps --format "{{.Names}}: {{.Status}}"
